To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
QS firms are not ready for BIM and are still in the process of understanding BIM, and are not clear about the benefits of BIM.

QS firms in Australia are not adopting BIM due to lack of knowledge about BIM, lack of information in the models, lack of clarity about BIM benefits, lack of support from clients, and lack of support from other consultants.
QS firms are not adopting BIM as a whole, they are only adopting parts of BIM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how BIM can improve the services provided by the QS firms and how QS firms are adopting BIM.
how well QS firms in Australia are increasing BIM and getting ready for the participation in BIM and how BIM is changing the QS services.
the adoption of BIM by QS firms in Australia and the implications for the construction industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adoption of BIM by QS firms has been slow and is not happening at the desired rate.

BIM adoption by quantity surveying firms is still in its early stage and the industry needs a more detailed research to identify the barriers for BIM adoption and to develop strategies for its successful adoption.
the adoption of BIM by QS firms in the form of take off is a slow process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BIM is a new technology that is not readily adopted in the QS firms.
the BIM adoption by quantity surveyors is slow and there is a need for more education and training to drive BIM adoption in the industry.

BIM is a new technology and it needs to be implemented in an incremental manner and the QS firms need to be trained to use BIM effectively and also to be trained to understand how BIM can help to increase the productivity and profitability of the firms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the construction industry needs to be more proactive in driving BIM adoption and in this regard, the QS firms need to be at the forefront.
the industry should focus more on BIM based working than BIM technology adoption.
BIM has the potential to improve efficiency of QS firms and to provide more accurate cost information to the construction industry.
